cards.text: Psalm 17 is a prayer of David, and he goes straight to the LORD. No small talk, no "Hey, how's Your week going?" He opens with this: "Hear, O LORD, my righteous plea; listen to my cry."

cards.question: David asks the LORD to give ear to his prayer. Where does he say that prayer comes from?

cards.text: Then David says, "May my vindication come from Your presence; may Your eyes see what is right." Not the neighbors, not the comment section, not the guy at work with OPINIONS: David wants the LORD's eyes on this one.

cards.question: David says the LORD has tried his heart and even visited him in the night. When God tested him, what did He find?
David says he has made up his mind not to sin with his mouth.

cards.text: David says that by the word of God's lips, he has avoided the ways of the violent. That's a man who sees trouble coming and crosses the street, then crosses it AGAIN just to be safe.

cards.question: David says his steps have held to God's paths, but his feet have slipped.

cards.text: David's feet have not slipped, while I'm attached to a gold base and I STILL wobble. Now David calls on God again, and he sounds completely sure of something.

cards.question: David calls on God because he's sure God will ___ him.

cards.text: David says, "Incline Your ear to me; hear my words." Then he asks God to show the wonders of His loving devotion, and friend, he's not asking for a sample, he wants the WHOLE cookie box.

cards.question: David says God saves people by His right hand. Which people?

answers.text: Those who seek refuge from their foes
Those who have never once stumbled
Those who bring the biggest offerings

cards.text: Then David paints two pictures: "Keep me as the apple of Your eye; hide me in the shadow of Your wings". Friend, that is NOT a man asking for a little personal space.

cards.question: David asks God to hide him in the shadow of His wings. Hide him from whom?

cards.text: David says these enemies have closed their callous hearts. Door shut, porch light off, and they're pretending nobody's home.

cards.question: David says his enemies speak with humility.

cards.text: And they don't just talk. David says they've tracked down him and the people with him, and now they surround them, like a bill collector who found your new number AND your new address.

cards.question: The enemies have David and the people with him surrounded. What are the enemies' eyes set on doing?

answers.text: Driving them out of the land

cards.text: Then David describes these enemies: "like a lion greedy for prey, like a young lion lurking in ambush." Me? The scariest thing that ever hunted me was a hand digging through the junk drawer for tape.

cards.question: David compares his enemies to a young lion lurking in ambush. What does that picture say about them?

answers.text: They are ready to make peace
They are tired of the fight

cards.text: So David cries out for the LORD to arise. When there's a lion lurking, you don't text a friend, you call on the LORD.

cards.question: David calls on the LORD to arise and confront the enemies surrounding him. What does he ask God to do to them?

answers.text: Lead them to make peace with him
Send them away to another land

cards.text: David asks God to deliver him by His sword and by His hand from men of the world whose portion is in this life. Everything they're after is right here, right now, like a baker who eats the whole batch before the box ever gets sealed.

cards.question: David asks God to fill the bellies of His treasured ones.
David keeps praying for God's treasured ones and their sons. What does he say gets left to the children?

cards.text: Then David turns the spotlight on himself: "As for me, I will behold Your face in righteousness". Those other guys can keep their portion in this life, friend, David wants to see God's FACE.

cards.question: David says that when he wakes up, he'll be ___ in God's presence.
